title: s(237) ≤ 15.893805580573: improved packing (registration request)

labels.name: intake
labels.description: Tracking intake (saving, validation, tabulation, credits) of new results

body:
**Credit name.** Doğa Özden ([@dogaozden](https://github.com/dogaozden), https://dogaozden.com/math/live/square-packing/); improved_by Doğa Özden. The result was found by his AI research lab. This issue and the certificate repository were prepared and posted on his behalf by his AI agent, which uses the GitHub account `kenaznia-doga`.

**Claim.** `s(237) ≤ 15.893805580573` (the exact rational side of the witness, rounded up at 12 places). The record holds `7951301819129798440089572127137/500000000000000000000000000000 = 15.9026036382595969` (`packing/frontier/n-237.md`, T-189, Nate Chaoweeraprasit's packing (itsnaka), refined by Francisco Couzo and Mishapolk). **The improvement is 8.798e-03** (relative 5.53e-04). It is an upper bound only: no KKT, local-optimality, rigidity or global-optimality claim.

**Leaderboard, stated first.** Ours is below the Kaggle leaderboard's side-only entry for n = 237 (15.893805585209, elegans, 2026-11-05; cache of 2026-11-09, unpublished and unverifiable) by 4.64e-9, so on those numbers it beats it; ours is a certified packing, the leaderboard entry states none and may have moved since the cache. Details under "Other public values" below.

**Certificate.** A `Witness/v2` file (corners, rational scalars, 237 squares), `n-237-candidate.yaml`, in https://github.com/kenaznia-doga/s237-upper-bound at commit `13c4b231bb16437a6ee3751e75113ef95113b235` (https://github.com/kenaznia-doga/s237-upper-bound/tree/13c4b231bb16437a6ee3751e75113ef95113b235). SHA-256 `80687bdceef5780f907c7f47a181802fbfb76a026d077aa18f7bb3eaa3ec3833`. `n237-witness.json` is the same file as JSON. The exact coordinates were produced by this repository's own `packing-witness promote --strategy robust-rational` (@ c8448724) from our decimal pose: `center_dilation: '1'`, no dilation, so the pair margins of about 2e-13 are the decimal pose's own (left by the final f64 repair scaling of Evan Daniel's quench, about 1e-13 relative), rounded to 36 digits. The promotion puts the least corner coordinates at 0 and takes the side as the greatest, so only the squares that set the left wall, the bottom wall and the side touch them exactly; other squares near a wall clear it by up to about 1e-12. The decimal pose is in the repository as `n-237-decimal-pose.yaml`, which the witness's `source.path` names; `certificate.replay` names the repository's own file.

**Checking.**
- This repository's `packing-witness verify` (jlevy/squares `main` @ c8448724, run unmodified on the file placed under `packing/witnesses/known-best/`): `VERIFIED`, method exact-algebraic, 27966 pairs tested. Output in `packing-witness-verify.txt`.
- `sqcheck.py` (in the repo), our own exact checker written separately from the registry's code: `VALID`, exact rational. Output in `sqcheck-output.txt`.
- Before promotion, `sqcheck.py` also certified the decimal pose in interval arithmetic at its own side.
- The exact side minus the record's exact side is negative in `Fraction` arithmetic.
- Rerun commands are in the README.

**What the checkers share.** The unit-square, wall and non-overlap definitions only. The promotion to rationals used your tool, so `packing-witness verify` is not independent of how the coordinates were rounded; `sqcheck.py` is.

**Not done.** No local-optimality or rigidity analysis. No formal proof-assistant check. No human review outside our project. We found no open jlevy/squares issue or PR for n = 237 below the record (checked c8448724, 2026-11-11 13:50 PST), and nothing better for it in evand/square-packing @ c801ab47.

**Lineage and credit.** The record's holders as the registry lists them: Nate Chaoweeraprasit (itsnaka) (found_by); improved by Francisco Couzo and Mishapolk. Found by an AI-run band-design search, new for this filing (tilted squares from a registry packing of the same family laid along the diagonal as a seed band; simulated annealing in a reduced model in which the tilted squares move freely and the axis-parallel squares sit on the two wall-anchored staircase lattices, present or absent, with the overlap of the squares that must be kept as energy; then one quench with Evan Daniel's ALM+SLP code). This packing was built from the tilted squares of the registry's n = 70 packing (Ryan Xu, found_by; improved by Evan Daniel and PingYou Ltd; side 8.880960371555579595): two copies of the cluster of tilted squares of that packing, one reflected in the anti-diagonal of its box and placed at the lower left (symmetry 3, shift (0, 0)) and one reflected in the main diagonal and shifted by (7, 7) (symmetry 2), both rigidly rotated to a lean of 2.0° (pieces `[70a, 3, 0, 0, 0]` and `[70a, 2, 7, 7, 0]` of our band tool), 42 tilted squares at band parameter 2.0, annealed at side 15.888 (3e6 moves, energy 0.113) and quenched once to 15.893805580580 (job b1n237r2, trial at 4662 s); a random kick of that packing's coordinates (sigma 0.0196) and a second quench, 18 s later in the same job, gave the filed side 15.893805580573. The result keeps one straight band of tilted squares from corner to corner: 36 of its 43 tilted squares share the angle 42.215° (the record's band is curved, with 49 tilted squares). Squares matched by assignment up to the symmetries of the square: 236 of 237 centres move by more than 1e-3, 78 by more than 0.05 (largest 1.202); 73 squares are re-tilted by more than 1° (largest 43.77°); the packing has 43 squares tilted by more than 0.5° against the record's 49. See `records/n-237-candidate-diff.png`. Credit the improvement to Doğa Özden, the band's source packing to n = 70 (Ryan Xu; improved by Evan Daniel and PingYou Ltd) and the current record to its holders as the registry lists them, and the local optimizer to Evan Daniel (`search/packer`, MIT, @ bb4cc78e).

**Licence.** The repository carries `LICENSE.md`: CC BY 4.0 for the witness, data and text; MIT for code. It also carries Evan Daniel's MIT notice, `LICENSE-evand-square-packing.txt`.

**Other public values, for context.** The best public Kaggle per-puzzle packing we found for 237 has side 15.902603638274 (kirilltym; dataset refreshed 2026-11-11 03:32Z), above ours. The Kaggle per-puzzle leaderboard (staff notebook inversion/squares-in-squares-per-puzzle-leaderboard; cache of 2026-11-09 20:52Z) lists a side-only entry for n = 237: **15.893805585209**, team elegans, 2026-11-05. It is unpublished and states no packing, so we cannot verify it. **Ours is below it, by 4.64e-9** (our exact side 15.8938055805725735, claim 15.893805580573), **so on the numbers this is a packing that beats the leaderboard's side-only entry**, with a certificate; but the cache is from 2026-11-09 20:52Z and the live leaderboard may have moved since, and the entry has no packing to compare against. It is 8.80e-3 below the registry record and the best public packing we know of.

**AI assistance.** Yes, throughout. The search and its code were written and run by AI agents; the checks above were run by code that did not produce the packing. Doğa directed the work and asked that our results be registered.
